content.title: About
content.content: Dried papaya consists of thin slices of ripe papaya (Carica papaya) that have been dehydrated. The process retains most of the fruit’s vitamins, minerals, and its characteristic sweet‑tart flavor. It is lightweight, shelf‑stable, and makes a convenient healthy snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Papaya originates from tropical Central and South America but is now cultivated in Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean.
Dried pieces are commonly used in muesli, granola, and energy bars.
Papaya contains the enzyme papain, which helps break down proteins.
Traditional medicine uses papaya to aid digestion and reduce inflammation.
When stored properly, dried papaya can last up to 12 months.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Dried papaya retains a high level of vitamin C, supporting the immune system and acting as an antioxidant.

items.title: Source of beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, essential for vision and skin health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The papain enzyme aids protein digestion, making it easier on the stomach.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements and helps you feel fuller longer.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Papaya provides potassium, magnesium, and iron, which are important for overall bodily functions.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to papaya.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Dried fruit concentrates natural sugars, so it should be consumed in moderation, especially by people with diabetes.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Some brands add preservatives; always check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried papaya can be eaten straight from the pack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, smoothies, or tossed into salads. For a softer texture, briefly soak in warm water before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, refrigerate. Discard if it becomes sticky, develops an off‑odor, or shows mold.
